headline: Austrian household power bills jump 34% — biggest rise on record
text:
# Austrian household power bills jump 34% — biggest rise on record

Energy dominates the page: record Austrian and Luxembourg electricity bills, the UK's last coal, Greece past 60% renewable power — while US chip prices run hot.

## Today in the data

### Austria's record electricity bill
[Household electricity price, EUR/kWh, all taxes (Eurostat nrg_pc_204)](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Austria paid EUR 0.3272/kWh in H2 2025, up 34.3% on a year earlier — the largest rise since the series starts in 2008 (energy-household-eu). Luxembourg, on the same chart, rose 31.7% to 0.2665. Both prices include all taxes, so the expiry of earlier relief measures is worth checking against; the usual yearly change is about 2.5%.

### US chip prices run 12% hotter
[US chip prices and chip output, year-on-year %](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Factory-gate prices for computer and electronic products rose 12.3% in the year to July 2026 (us-ppi-sectors), against a typical +0.6%. Chip output moved with it: semiconductor IP up 11.9% in the same month (us-chips). The IP index is quality-adjusted, so it rises with chip performance, not only with units.

### Bulgarian mining output halves
[Bulgaria: mining and quarrying output (Eurostat sts_inpr_m)](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Mining and quarrying stood at 50.3 (2021=100) in June 2026, down 48.3% on a year earlier — the sharpest fall in a record from 2001 (eu-mining-ipi). The chart shows the series is jumpy month to month, so a single low print can be revised. The July figure is due.

### The UK's last coal power
[UK electricity generation by source, TWh (Ember/EI via OWID)](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
UK coal generation fell 82.6% to 0.33 TWh in 2025, the sharpest drop in a record that starts in 1921 (electricity-mix). Wind produced 85.84 TWh and gas 90.91 TWh the same year — the crossing point is the thing to watch. The last year is often Ember's provisional figure.

### Greece past 60% renewable power
[Greece: renewable share of electricity (Eurostat nrg_ind_ren)](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Greece's renewable share of electricity reached 60.9% in 2025, up 9.65 points in a year — the biggest annual gain since 2005 (eu-renewables-share). The chart shows an almost unbroken climb from about 8% in 2004. These are Renewable Energy Directive accounting rules, so the figure differs from Ember's generation share.

### Estonia's car market halves
[New car registrations in Estonia by fuel (Eurostat road_eqr_carpda)](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Estonia registered 13,141 new cars in 2025, down 49% on 2024, with diesel down 70.4% to 1,738 (eu-car-registrations). Petrol, at 10,531, took the fall too, so this looks like a market-wide contraction rather than a fuel switch; electric was 872. The record starts only in 2013.

### Egypt's FDI falls back
[Egypt: net FDI inflows, current US dollars (World Bank WDI)](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Net FDI inflows were $15.45bn in 2025, $31.1bn below 2024 — the sharpest fall since 1971 (macro-external). The chart makes clear it is a base effect: 2024's $46.6bn spike is the outlier, and 2025 is close to the pre-spike trend. WDI figures lag and get revised.

## Numbers desk

### Forecasts
- **us-ppi-sectors · computer_electronic** last 118.276 (2026-07) → 119.6 by 2026-09, band 118.5–120.8, Holt-Winters additive. In-sample MAPE 0.27%; a trend extrapolation, not a demand model.
- **eu-mining-ipi · BG|B** last 50.3 (2026-06) → 63.0 by 2026-09, band 32.4–93.6, Holt-Winters additive. The band is wider than the level; treat as uninformative.
- **energy-household-eu · AT** last 0.3272 (2025-S2) → 0.3249 by 2026-S2, band 0.2904–0.3594, Holt-Winters additive. Half-yearly data, 37 observations only.

### Correlations
- **AT vs LU household power prices** (yoy, 2008-S2–2025-S2, n=35): r = 0.64, lag +4 half-years, clears the band but so do lag −1 (0.61) and lag 0 (0.53) — read the contemporaneous one.
- **US semiconductor IP vs computer/electronic PPI** (yoy, 2010-01–2026-07, n=199): r = −0.26, lag +3 months, not distinguishable from zero (Bartlett band 0.45).

## What to watch
- **eu-mining-ipi**: July 2026 settles whether Bulgaria's 50.3 was a one-month outage or a level shift.
- **us-ppi-sectors** and **us-chips**: August data show whether 12% chip-price inflation is still accelerating.
- **cpi-eu / eu-hicp**: July 2026 releases test whether record power bills are reaching headline inflation.
- **cattle-eu** (last 2026-08) and **cattle-us / corn-parity** (2026-07): the next prints refresh the meat-price chain.
- **eu-air-passengers** and **eu-tourism-nights**: due for June–July 2026, the summer season's first read.

## Sources
- energy-household-eu — Eurostat nrg_pc_204, last 2025-S2.
- us-ppi-sectors — BLS producer price indexes by NAICS industry via FRED, last 2026-07.
- us-chips — Federal Reserve industrial production via FRED, last 2026-07.
- eu-mining-ipi — Eurostat sts_inpr_m, last 2026-06.
- electricity-mix — Ember Yearly Electricity Data and Energy Institute, via Our World in Data, last 2025.
- eu-renewables-share — Eurostat nrg_ind_ren, last 2025.
- eu-car-registrations — Eurostat road_eqr_carpda, last 2025.
- macro-external — World Bank World Development Indicators, last 2025.
